html:
The Siege of Geok Tepe was the Russian attack on the Teke Turkmen fortress of Geok Tepe, near Ashgabat in Turkmenistan, which fell on 24 January 1881 after weeks of siege.

The Teke had beaten a Russian force there in 1879. General Mikhail Skobelev came back with artillery and a railway, the start of the Trans-Caspian Railway. Russian sappers blew a hole in the walls. Thousands of defenders and people inside died in the storming and the pursuit that followed.

Russia went on to found Ashgabat and take Merv in 1884, bringing the Turkmen lands into the Russian Empire, a move that alarmed Britain in the Great Game. In independent Turkmenistan the battle is mourned each year as a day of national memory, and a mosque now stands at the site.
